_headline: Highest BOD at Hansol, where the Sabarmati enters the city: 1.2 to 5 mg/L across 2018-2024. At V.N. Bridge, below the city's outfalls: 82 to 358 mg/L.

rivers.name: Sabarmati
rivers.cpcb_class: Priority I in the 2018, 2022 and 2025 editions (BOD above 30 mg/L)
rivers.description: Clean where it enters Ahmedabad and among India's most polluted stretches where it leaves. Through the city the river is a 15 km reach held by the Vasna barrage and topped up from the Narmada canal; below the barrage it carries the city's treated and untreated sewage and the industrial effluent of the Mega pipeline and the Narol CETP.
rivers.notes: CPCB's polluted-stretch definition has narrowed in each edition: Kheroj to Vautha (2018, BOD 4 to 147 mg/L), Raysan to Vautha (2022, maximum 292 mg/L at V.N. Bridge), V.N. Bridge to the confluence at Vautha (October 2025, maximum 105 mg/L). Readings at 0.3 mg/L dissolved oxygen are CPCB's detection floor, i.e. effectively none.

rivers.name: Khari
rivers.cpcb_class: Priority I in the 2018, 2022 and 2025 editions
rivers.description: A tributary that runs past the industrial estates on the city's eastern edge and joins the Sabarmati downstream. CPCB monitors it at one point, Lali village.
rivers.notes: Maximum BOD in CPCB's polluted-stretch editions: 235 mg/L (2018), 195 (2022), 68 (2025).
